rules_that_are_not_obvious: Real integration first; the mock is written afterwards and copies observed behaviour.
The docs site and apps/app come LAST — they consume the packages, so building them early hides which package does not work.
Nothing is dropped for time. If it cannot be built to the bar it ships declared unbuilt.
Never cd into sources/ — the harness resolves the project root from the shell cwd, and the stage guard will block source writes.

Never cd into a package directory: the stage guard resolves the project root from the shell cwd, so `cd packages/core` makes it infer stage=orient and block every source write. Use pnpm --filter from the root.

The test lock unlocks one edit PER TEST FILE per SPEC.md write — it compares each file's mtime to SPEC.md's, so one SPEC.md write unlocks every test file, but only once each. Batch test edits behind one real SPEC.md change; never touch SPEC.md just to unlock.
SPEC.md's '## Files' section ends at the next heading of ANY depth — a ### subheading inside it hides everything below from the scope guard.
react-ui imports @flare-kit/react from dist, so a hook change needs pnpm build before react-ui tests see it.

applyTransition SILENTLY DROPS ITS PATCH when the transition is not allowed by the table in states.ts. A reconciler that jumps states loses its step updates with no error and no failing test — fdc/operation.ts walks the table with a breadth-first search for exactly this reason. Any future reconciler must do the same.

Relay.isFinalized returning true does NOT mean the proof can be fetched. The data availability layer indexes the round minutes later. Poll retrieveProof; never conclude 'no proof' from a single absence.
The FDC request fee is 1000 wei on Coston2 and 20 FLR on mainnet (3 FLR for ConfirmedBlockHeightExists). Never hardcode it.

The verifier's OpenAPI and the on-chain fee configuration are two independent oracles for what a deployment serves, and they disagree about Web2Json on mainnet. Checking only the route would report an unsubmittable family as supported.

FTSO: FtsoV2.verifyFeedData REVERTS on a bad proof where FdcVerification.verifyEVMTransaction returns false. The two protocols must NOT share a boolean verification abstraction — catching the revert and coercing it to false renders 'we could not check this' as 'this is not proven'.
FTSO: decimals are per READING, not per feed. FLR/USD is 6 on the anchor path and 8 on the block-latency path. Never cache decimals per feed and never share them between the two paths.

FTSO: the anchor-feed DA returns HTTP 200 with an EMPTY ARRAY for an unknown feed id, and only 400 for a non-retained round. fdc/client.ts checks status only, which is correct for FDC and a silent failure here. Check array length and per-feed presence.

FTSO: the Relay's Merkle root OUTLIVES the DA's leaves, so committed-on-chain-but-no-longer-retrievable is a real first-class state. BUT the recorded floor of 1130919 / ~297 days is WRONG — measured 2026-08-05, round 1130919 retrieves a value and the boundary is around 818368, roughly twice the window.
FTSO: enumerate with getSupportedFeedIds(), never getFeedIds() — the latter is a storage array with recycled slots and returns 64 entries including an unused zero feed id at index 52.

FTSO: a custom feed id is 0x21 ++ ASCII name right-zero-padded to 21 bytes. developer-hub/docs/ftso/guides/create-custom-feed.mdx:75,147 documents 0x21 + keccak256(name) and is WRONG — every deployed feed disproves it.

FTSO: reads are payable and free TODAY but that is not a property of the surface — fetchAllCurrentFeeds() already costs 1 wei because the unused slot falls through to defaultFee(). Quote calculateFeeByIds; never assume zero.

FTSO: a Fast Update incentive's effect DECAYS. Confirmation must read getRange() at the transaction's own block against the preceding one, not a later block. A late read showing no effect is not a failed offer.

FTSO: getFeedsById SILENTLY RESOLVES A RENAMED ID to its current feed — getFeedsById([MATIC/USD, POL/USD]) returns 74335 for BOTH on Coston2. FTSO: viem's readContract has NO value parameter — passing one is silently dropped. Payable views must go through simulateContract or the call goes out with 0 and reverts wherever the fee is non-zero.

mock-ftso.ts is a READER the real core functions are driven by, not a second implementation. It also refuses to answer anything it never observed, so an unmocked call is a loud error rather than a plausible zero. It is the only way to test the paid-read path, since the Coston2 fee is 0.

DEX/BlazeSwap: the router addLiquidity is NOT standard UniswapV2 — it inserts two extra uint256 params, feeBipsA and feeBipsB (fee-on-transfer tolerance, 0 for standard tokens), BETWEEN amountBMin and `to`. The standard 8-param selector (0xe8e33700) hits the router fallback and reverts with EMPTY data. removeLiquidity and swapExactTokensForTokens ARE standard. Authoritative signature: sources/flare-foundation/fasset-bots/packages/fasset-liquidator/contracts/interfaces/IUniswapV2/IUniswapV2Router.sol; Flare's own liquidator passes feeBipsA=0, feeBipsB=0. Caught only by the live add run (empty-revert + a sibling call working = an ABI/selector mismatch, not a logic bug). NOTE: a future mainnet (SparkDEX V2) add path may use the STANDARD signature — adds are venue-specific, unlike swap/remove, so the shared UNIV2_ROUTER_ABI can't serve both networks for addLiquidity when that path is built.

DEX: a V2 add mints min(amountA*ts/rA, amountB*ts/rB) LP (Uniswap V2 mint()), NOT amountA*ts/rA — with real reserves the two differ by ~1 wei from floor-division, so predicting lpFromA overstates by a wei and breaks predicted==minted. The kit's quoteAddLiquidity uses the min; the live run confirmed lpMinted == predictedLp exactly. LP token decimals for a V2 pair are 18 (UniswapV2ERC20 constant), independent of the pool tokens' decimals; expected LP renders as an Amount at 18dp (this BlazeSwap pair's LP symbol is BLAZE-LP).

VAULTS/Upshift: deposit is NON-standard — deposit(address assetIn, uint256 amountIn, address receiver), asset-address FIRST (not ERC-4626 deposit(assets,receiver)); previewDeposit(asset,amount) and previewRedemption(shares,isInstant) return TWO values incl. a contract-computed assetsAfterFee. The kit renders assetsAfterFee (contract-computed) as the honest net received, per route. The share/LP token is a SEPARATE ERC20 at lpTokenAddress() (vFXRP on Coston2, earnXRP on Flare mainnet — probe the symbol, never guess). Withdraw/instant PULL the LP so they need an LP approve; Firelight self-share redeem needs none.

VAULTS/Firelight: the standard ERC-4626 maxDeposit RETURNS uint256 MAX and does NOT reflect the vault custom GLOBAL depositLimit — a deposit within maxDeposit still reverts DepositLimitExceeded() (0x6adf7e28) once totalAssets reaches depositLimit. Measured live 2026-08-11: depositLimit 15000000, totalAssets 14994061 → only 5939 units (0.005939 FXRP) of real headroom. availability() must cap at min(maxDeposit, depositLimit-totalAssets). Firelight withdraw/redeem are DELAYED period-based requests (no immediate transfer); claimWithdraw(period) after currentPeriodEnd. The FIRST redeem in a period does extra checkpoint writes — buffer gas ~1.5x or it goes out-of-gas (an estimate taken right after the deposit undercounts; the tx replays fine via eth_call, confirming gas not logic).

VAULTS/lifecycle: a vault delayed withdrawal needs NO new operation state — it maps onto the existing canonical states awaiting_external (period/epoch clock) -> action_required (claimable, via escalate with a safe claim action, movesNewValue:false) -> succeeded. Same shape as M3 FDC proof wait. withdrawVerified (per vault, per network) is the M7 analog of dex.ts addLiquidityVerified: buildWithdrawPlan refuses an unverified withdraw path without reading or approving anything.

M8/LayerZero: Coston2's RPC caps eth_getLogs to ~30 blocks, so a delivery reconcile that scans from the submit block over a multi-minute wait MUST chunk into ≤25-block ranges or the read reverts. Sepolia tolerated a wide range and hid this; chunking is correct on both. bridge-adapter.ts scanByGuid does it.

M8/FAssets redeem: FAssetRedeemed on the composer is the redemption REQUEST filed, NOT 'XRP received' — the FAssets agent pays XRPL separately (same as M1's redeem: nothing is done until the protocol settles). The op reaches succeeded ONLY from the XRPL settlement read. The reconciler has THREE legs, all awaiting_external distinguished by actor: executor (LZ delivery) → flare (FAssets filed) → xrpl (agent paying). A first cut that concluded succeeded from FAssetRedeemed alone was the milestone's own honesty class and was caught in review.

M8/lifecycle: a reconciler that advances `awaiting` but never advanceSteps leaves a succeeded op's spine steps 'pending', which OperationTimeline draws as 'outcome unknown' — and the spine renders on succeeded (card-chrome IN_FLIGHT includes succeeded). Terminal reconciles MUST finalize steps AND clear the descriptor with {awaiting: undefined} — applyPatch only clears a key that is EXPLICITLY present, so an undefined whole-patch leaves a settled op still claiming it waits on somebody.

M8/XRPL settlement correlation: the redeemer's XRPL address also receives faucet drops, so matching 'the most recent incoming Payment' false-positives the redeem success. Correlate on delivered_amount ≈ redeemedAmountUBA (net of the agent fee, e.g. ≥95%) AND a ledger date that postdates the redemption filing.

M8/lot size: the cross-chain redeem's FAssets leg is lot-based (1 lot = 10 FXRP on Coston2, lotSizeXRP 10). Verifying it live needs ≥ 1 lot on the SOURCE chain first — a 1-FXRP bridge cannot be redeemed. Phase A bridged 1 FXRP (the AC1 gate); a top-up bridged 9 more before the redeem.

M8/OFT: the type-3 executor option OMITS the value word when it is 0 (16-byte lzReceive payload, 18-byte lzCompose payload). The FXRP OFT route removes NO dust (sharedDecimals 6, decimalConversionRate 1) so amountReceivedLD == amountSentLD; a stale RPC once returned 0 balance for a funded Sepolia account (the never-conclude-from-a-single-absence rule again).

M7/Firelight: a delayed redeem in period P files its withdrawal under period P+1 (the UNLOCK period), and claimWithdraw(P+1) is callable only once currentPeriod > P+1. Recording the REQUEST period P strands the claim: withdrawalsOf(P)=0 and claimWithdraw(P) reverts (0x95dece8d). The claim ref period is currentPeriod+1, claimable at nextPeriodEnd (read at request time). Encoded in firelightClaimRef(); caught live 2026-08-12 when the Phase-A ref recorded period 333 but the withdrawal was at 334. Upshift is calendar-epoch, NOT off-by-one.

M9/EIP-712: the deployed forwarder domain ('GaslessPaymentForwarder','1') and MockUSDT0 domain ('Mock USDT0','1') are byte-identical to their on-chain DOMAIN_SEPARATOR; core reproduces both OFFLINE (viem hashDomain, asserted in tests). That domain-separator EQUALITY is a far stronger 'single source of truth' test than a sign->recover round-trip, which passes even when the domain is self-consistently wrong.

M9/receipts: viem waitForTransactionReceipt RESOLVES for a mined-but-REVERTED tx (it only rejects on timeout/replacement). A settle/relay that passes the pre-send simulateContract can still revert when mined (the double-settle race: two requests with the same EIP-3009 authorization both pass verify+simulate; the first consumes the nonce, the second reverts 'authorization used'). Gate success on receipt.status==='success', or a reverted settlement is dressed as settled->succeeded. The M9 live scripts had the check; the SHIPPED server/relayer did NOT - caught by the honesty review subagent, not by any test.

M9/x402: the x402 server MUST bind the authorization's `to` to the configured payee before settling (settlePayment is unbound, unlike the facilitator's settlePaymentAsPayee). Without it a payer signs a self-transfer (from=to=attacker), the facilitator settles a net-zero transfer, and the server hands over the paid resource for free (the M9 security review's payee-bypass).

M9/services: Express 4 does NOT catch a rejected async handler - an unauthenticated malformed input (a bad X-Payment header) becomes an unhandled rejection that can crash the process. Wrap service handlers in try/catch AND strictly type-validate decoded payload fields (not just truthiness) before BigInt()/toLowerCase() touch them.

M9/viem: passing a bare ADDRESS STRING as simulateContract({account}) makes viem treat it as a node-signed (json-rpc) account, so writeContract(sim.request) then goes out via eth_sendTransaction and a node without the key rejects it ('Missing or invalid parameters'). Pass the LOCAL Account object (walletClient.account) so the request local-signs (eth_sendRawTransaction).

M9/gas: Coston2 base gas spiked to ~650 gwei during the live run (~26x the usual ~25). A native-transfer drain-to-~0 must compute its fee from an explicit legacy gasPrice + gas=21000, not an EIP-1559 maxFee estimate, or the tx fails 'gas required exceeds allowance' (the remaining balance covers 21000*gasPrice but not 21000*maxFeePerGas).

M9/gasless-not-free: the one-time approve(forwarder) is the ONLY step the payer pays gas for; every payment after it is gasless (the relayer bears the gas). The proof is 'payer NATIVE balance UNCHANGED across the payment', not 'payer balance is 0' - the payer never sends the payment tx so its balance is untouched regardless; draining to ~0 is corroborating, not the proof.

M9/EIP-3009 substrate: neither FXRP nor the real Coston2 USD-T0 dispatches any EIP-3009 selector (re-probed 2026-08-12), so x402 has no real-token substrate on testnet - it runs on a self-deployed MockUSDT0 whose demoToken flag is REGISTRY DATA (never a hand-typed label that could drift), and the client derives 'is this a demo token' from the registry by ADDRESS, never from the server's (untrusted) asset string.

M9/reconcile: reconcileTo/waitSince/advance now live in packages/core/src/reconcile.ts, shared by the bridge/gasless/x402 reconcilers - the applyTransition-silently-drops-its-patch hazard is handled in ONE place. Any new capability reconciler imports these, never re-implements the table walk.

M10/Flare delegation: `delegate` != delegation — a delegate op reaches `succeeded` ONLY from the on-chain `delegatesOf` read reflecting the target, NEVER from the send. Undelegate succeeded = delegatesOf empty; wrap succeeded = wrappedBalance reflects the wrap.

M10/Flare: percentage vs explicit (AMOUNT) delegation are MODE-EXCLUSIVE — a percentage `delegate` while the account is in AMOUNT mode (or vice-versa) SILENTLY NO-OPS on-chain. The plan refuses it (mode-conflict) and the card reads 'undelegate first', never emitting the no-op call. `delegationModeOf` NEVER resets to NOTSET once set, so exercising AMOUNT on a single signer permanently blocks its PERCENTAGE path.

M10/Flare: WNat.withdraw writes a COLD vote-power-checkpoint SSTORE that `eth_estimateGas` UNDER-COUNTS right after an undelegate — the tx simulates clean but the mined tx OOG-REVERTS (status:'reverted', not a decode error; happened twice 300 blocks apart). FIX: set an explicit generous gas limit on WNat/vote-power-checkpoint-writing calls. Simulate-clean != execution-clean. (Carry to M11 staking — same WNat/vote-power surface.)

M10/Flare rewards honesty: RNat.getBalancesOf REVERTS 'no RNat account' (not (0,0,0)) and DistributionToDelegators.getClaimableMonths REVERTS 'already finished' (FlareDrop concluded 2026-01-30). A CONTRACT REVERT maps to a DECLARED honest-empty state; a TRANSPORT/network error must RETHROW (unknown != empty — a dead RPC must never render as 'no rNat').

M10/Flare rewards shapes: getRewardEpochIdsWithClaimableRewards returns a (start,end) RANGE tuple, NOT a list; getStateOfRewards returns tuple[][] whose inner RewardState has 5 fields incl. `bool initialised` — DISTINCT from claim()'s 4-field RewardClaim (no bool). claimableEpochs must be gated on FlareSystemsManager.rewardsHash(epoch)!=0 (the signed-epoch gate). Delegation-reward expiry is 25 epochs; staking rewards do NOT expire — never one 'rewards expire' line.

M10 process: a verified-flag flip (delegationVerified false->true) BREAKS gate tests whose fixture used the registry DEFAULT — use an EXPLICIT verified/unverified fixture, and after ANY flip re-run the FULL suite (not just the flipped package). Run ROOT `pnpm lint` in the gate: zero-width-space chars + script no-undef (e.g. AbortController in .mjs) only surface there, not in per-package build/typecheck/test.

Only the controller ADDRESS is a constant.

The Smart Accounts vault registry is its OWN id->address namespace and on Coston2 it points at DIFFERENT deployments from M7's. Controller Coston2 vaults: TESTstXRP 0xD91324A6…0B5b, TESTearnXRP 0x9E63a5D2…8319, TESTstXRP 0x4066A136…355E, stXRP 0xC90D6847…0361 — none is M7's Coston2 Firelight 0x91Bfe6A6…E40B or Upshift 0x24c1a47c…7C81. On MAINNET they overlap (controller vault id 2 IS M7's earnXRP 0x373D7d20…dEA28). Resolve vault ids from getVaults(), NEVER from vaults.ts.

The instruction-type nibble IS the vault-type enum: Instructions.sol calls Vault.deposit(pa, IVaultsFacet.VaultType(instructionType), vault, amount) and VaultType is None=0, Firelight=1, Upshift=2 — identical to instruction types FXRP=0, Firelight=1, Upshift=2. A Firelight instruction pointed at an Upshift vault id must be refused at PLAN time, not left to revert.

PaymentProofs.verifyPayment enforces block.timestamp <= paymentProofValidityDurationSeconds + responseBody.blockTimestamp. Past that the instruction can NEVER execute while the XRP has already reached the operator's wallet — a first-class terminal expiry state that must state where the funds are and that paying again is a NEW payment, never a retry (R-SA-008). The window differs by 12x between networks (24h Coston2, 2h mainnet).

The 32-byte payment reference has COMMAND-DEPENDENT, OVERLAPPING tail windows: bytes 12-13 agentVaultId (uint16), 14-15 vaultId (uint16), OR 12-31 a 20-byte address for FXRP transfer. A decoder that reads every field unconditionally is wrong — dispatch on the command. PaymentReferenceParser also REVERTS on value==0, agentVaultId==0, vaultId==0 and the zero address.

InstructionExecuted indexes personalAccount, transactionId AND paymentReference — the OPPOSITE of M1's direct-minting events, which index nothing (hence the standing 'decode the receipt, never a topic filter' rule). Here a topic filter is correct and is what makes R-SA-009's backfill-from-a-safe-boundary watcher possible. The rule is per-event, not global.
executeDirectMintingWithData (the 0xFE hash-commitment path, M14) is NOT in the vendored ABI; executeDirectMinting (which serves 0xFF) IS.

XRPL transactions targeting smart accounts must carry NO DestinationTag — a tag forces FAssets minting to credit the tag-holder and lets an unrelated party front-run the user operation. M1's xrpl.ts already encodes this rule for its own reason.

executeInstruction is PERMISSIONLESS both ways: the same property that lets this kit be its own operator lets the OPERATOR'S backend dispatch your payment first. Observed live 2026-08-13 on the M13 deposit run — our proof reached a payment already consumed and the call reverted TransactionAlreadyExecuted(); 0xca0bf4cbc1cf8c4b5fd7984b42af907099084466 had dispatched it at block 34022984. The plan's replay gate CANNOT close this: it reads isTransactionIdUsed before the payment, and the race happens after. Re-check isTransactionIdUsed immediately before submitting and treat a used id as 'someone else dispatched it, go read the effect' rather than an error. The core reconciler already handles this correctly by design — instructionExecuted comes from a READ, not from our submission, so an operation still reaches succeeded when a third party dispatched it.

protocol_gotchas_m12: GovernanceVotePower is a DIFFERENT contract from M10 FTSO vote power. delegate(to) is all-or-nothing to ONE address; there is no bips form. It is also NOT IClaimSetupManager.delegateGovernance, which is a claim-executor feature on another contract entirely.
GovernanceVotePower.delegate sets a POINTER and succeeds at 0 governance VP — no WNat wrap or balance is required to move the delegate, which is why the M12 round trip cost nothing but gas.

PollingFtso.isMember REVERTS for a non-member address rather than returning false. Any eligibility read must surface it as undefined; coercing the revert to false invents a negative answer the chain never gave.

There are TWO different proposal-state enums, and they disagree at the same index. FTSO (IPollingFtso.sol): Canceled=0, Pending=1, Active=2, Defeated=3, Succeeded=4. Foundation (IGovernor.sol): Pending=0, Active=1, Defeated=2, Succeeded=3, Queued=4, Expired=5, Executed=6, Canceled=7. Index 3 means Defeated on FTSO and Succeeded on Foundation — decoding with the wrong table inverts the outcome. Dispatch on a source discriminator.

The deployed PollingFtso getProposalInfo shape carries NO votePowerBlock, NO hasVoted and NO per-voter getVotes. Those fields must stay undefined and render as "—"; the vendored IGovernor interface is NOT the deployed FTSO shape.

Proposal discovery must respect the Flare eth_getLogs range cap and page in bounded windows. Real foundation proposals are MONTHS apart while any sane scan window is hours, so a bounded event scan legitimately returns nothing on mainnet — getLastProposal is the only read that actually surfaces the live proposal.

An empty array from proposal discovery is a CLAIM ("the read succeeded and the chain has none"), not the absence of an answer. A catch that swallows a failed read into [] therefore fabricates a statement about the chain even though it fabricates no data. M12 shipped this bug and the review gate caught it: discovery now throws and the hook keeps undefined (unavailable) distinct from [] (confirmed-empty).

A no-op write reaches succeeded off PRE-EXISTING state. Re-delegating to the address you already delegate to makes the read-back match immediately, so the reconciler confirms an operation whose transaction may never have landed. Refuse no-ops at the PLAN, where the pre-state is known, not at the reconciler, which cannot tell two identical reads apart.

applyTransition DROPS its patch on an illegal state hop and returns the record unchanged. A test fixture that jumps an illegal edge therefore silently produces steps:[], and every steps.every(...) assertion written against it is VACUOUSLY true — including assertions written specifically to guard dropped patches. Fixtures must walk the legal path and assert they arrived.
m13_lessons: Two worth carrying. (1) A WRONG COMMENT BECAME A WRONG NUMBER ON SCREEN: adapter.ts listed mainnet ids 0x00/0x02/0x10/0x20/0x23 at 950000 drops; the probe says 0x23 is 500000 — four ids, not five. The mock copied the SENTENCE instead of the JSON, so the gallery rendered a fabricated chain read on the screen whose purpose is showing fees are read. It reached six places and the sixth was a TEST asserting the fabricated number — a test can hold a bug still. When recording an observed value, copy from the evidence file, never from prose about it. (2) THREE ASSERTIONS COULD NOT FAIL, including toContain('0 drops') passing off an unrelated '1000 drops' fee row, leaving the milestone's headline honesty rule with no falsifiable coverage. Substring assertions over whole-card text are worthless for these rules: scope to the row, use exact equality, then mutation-check.

(b) NINE OperationTimeline callers still leak the wall clock into RecoveryPanel (Deposit, Bridge, Stake, Claim, Swap, X402, Delegation, Gasless, Governance cards). WithdrawCard is FIXED — it was the one place the bug was already live, its recovery being gated by the claim window. The nine carry no clock prop at all, so fixing them is an API change across nine published components: not taken unasked.
